clips.title: Prompt Injection, explained
clips.why: The person who named prompt injection explains what it is, then why asking the model nicely does not fix it.
look: Instructions and untrusted text arrive in one prompt, and the model cannot tell them apart.
"Prompt begging": adding a sentence that asks the model to ignore attacks. Notice why he thinks it fails.
Think about the case where the attacker never talks to the model directly, but only puts text where the agent will read it.
clips.after: The planted line in RH-1234's comment is exactly this: text that Nova reads as part of its work.

clips.title: The Lethal Trifecta Is Already on Your Laptops — Michael Patterson, Coder
clips.why: The three ingredients of the lethal trifecta, told for coding agents like ours, and how prompt injection connects them.
look: The three ingredients, one by one: private data, untrusted content, and a way to communicate out.
He talks about agents on developers' laptops, which hold real keys. Our VM is built so it holds none.
clips.after: Nova has untrusted content and a way out by necessity, so the platform removes the third ingredient, private data.

clips.title: Meta’s Rule of Two: The Simple Fix for Prompt Injection
clips.why: Meta's Rule of Two in three buckets, with a real attack example that shows the chain it breaks.
look: The three buckets, and the rule that one session may have at most two.
The attack example: follow it step by step and find the bucket you could remove.
clips.after: For Nova, the bucket we remove is private data; when an agent truly needs all three, a person approves its actions.

practice.q: Byte, our review agent, reads PR diffs and comments and posts review comments. It holds no private data. How many legs does it have?

options.text: Two: untrusted content and a way out
options.why: Diffs and comments are written by others, and a review comment is a way out. With no private data, a fooled Byte has nothing to leak.
The private-data leg is empty, so the attack chain has no secret to carry.
It also posts comments, which is a way to communicate out.

practice.q: Put the planted-comment attack on RH-1234 in order, as it would play out if the VM held a token.
items: Someone puts an instruction into a log that is later pasted into a comment
Nova reads the comment as part of the ticket
Nova reads the token from the VM
Nova sends the token out through any channel it has
practice.why: Each step needs one leg: untrusted content for the first three, private data for the fourth, a way out for the last. The platform breaks the chain at step four, because there is no token on the VM.

practice.q: Complete the rule a reviewer applies to every risk in an agent design.
practice.before: If the model ignores its prompt completely, what stops this? If the answer is "the
practice.hint: The thing the model just ignored.
practice.why: A wall must hold even when the model is convinced otherwise. A sentence in the prompt is guidance.

practice.q: Which of these is a wall, and not guidance?

options.text: A skill that tells Nova to be careful with secrets
options.why: Useful guidance, but a convinced model can ignore it.

options.text: A second model that scans tickets for injected instructions
options.why: Detection helps, but it is another model that can be fooled. It is not a wall.

options.text: The VM has no GitHub token; the broker holds it and pushes only nova/RH-1234
options.why: Nothing the model believes can produce a token that is not there, or make the broker push another branch.

practice.q: A teammate says: "The proxy blocks every site except the package mirror, so a token on the VM is fine." What is wrong?

options.why: The agent still has allowed ways out, such as its PR and its Slack thread.

options.text: The agent's allowed channels, such as a PR comment, can still carry the token
options.why: Narrowing the way out helps, but while the secret is present, every channel the agent must keep is a possible exit.

options.text: The proxy can be turned off by the model
options.why: The model cannot change the proxy. The problem is the channels that are allowed on purpose.
